experiment: Hoist active ProgramId out of the per-opcode dispatch loop, updating it only after a tail call changes programs
decision: reject for the current Linux V8-v7 source: the 11-pair Splay Score interval is entirely negative and RSS includes a tie, despite earlier M4 instruction-count gains on microloops

source.delta: Capture the executing frame ProgramId once before the dispatch loop; refresh it after StepResult::TailCall, eliminating the per-op frame program read while retaining cross-program tail-call lookup.

v2_m4_reference.finding: 11 alternating pairs reduced retired instructions by 2.00% on a CJS local-store loop and 1.40% on a CJS call loop; RSS median fell 180,224 bytes on both. These microloops did not establish V8-v7 Score effects.

node_oracle.50k_control: Baseline and candidate Quench both produced identical output for 50,000 strict tail calls. Node v24.19.0 overflowed its ordinary call stack at that depth, so it was not used as an oracle for this control.

wasm.command: WASM_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 cargo run --profile iteration -p quench-wasm-test --bin run -- --report <report> crates/quench-wasm-test/testsuite/return_call.wast crates/quench-wasm-test/testsuite/return_call_indirect.wast

correctness.full_test262_stage_campaign: not run because the candidate was rejected by its paired V8-v7 Score result
